newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Prostitutes, transvestites, police clash in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Prostitutes, transvestites, police clash in Bogota.

text.p: Prostitutes, transvestites and police fought a running battle along one of the main streets of an upscale area of northern Bogota early Saturday, according to a Reuters correspondent who witnessed the confrontation.

Police repeatedly fired volleys of pistol shots into the air as the sex workers responded with a hail of bricks and masonry from a nearby building site. Pedestrians, making their way home from bars in the fashionable Zona Rosa nightclub district scurried for cover and the street was blocked to traffic.

"These transvestites and prostitutes are drugged and began smashing up cars. We have arrested six or seven of them," Col. Luis Alberto Garcia, of the Bogota police, told the Reuters correspondent at the scene.

The fighting lasted for at least half-an-hour but ended after about 40 police agents rounded up some 30 sex workers near the entrance of a shopping mall and began kicking, punching them and beating them with nightsticks.

One of the prostitutes, 25-year-old Geraldin, admitted she and her colleagues had smashed the windows of a number of cars but only after motorists blocked their passage as they tried to flee from police.
Police frequently make sweeps through the area, which is a commercial and fashionable residential zone. They particularly target transvestites, whom they accuse of being troublemakers and thieves.
